stem: Varga Industries has net income of USD 120 million and 40 million shares trading at USD 60. It plans to use USD 240 million of cash, currently earning 3% pre-tax, to repurchase shares at the market price. The tax rate is 30%. EPS after the repurchase is closest to:
explanation: Shares repurchased = 240 / 60 = 4 million; remaining 36 million. Lost after-tax interest = 240 × 0.03 × 0.70 = 5.04 million. EPS = (120 − 5.04) / 36 = 3.19.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 3.33 = 120 / 36 ignores the interest income forgone on the cash used.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 3.13 deducts the pre-tax interest of 7.2 million instead of the after-tax 5.04 million.
rationale.C: Correct. (120 − 5.04) / 36 = 3.19, higher than 3.00 because the 5% earnings yield exceeds the 2.1% after-tax yield on cash.

stem: A company operates under a double taxation system with a corporate tax rate of 30%. Its shareholders pay a 20% tax on dividends. The effective tax rate on a unit of pre-tax corporate earnings distributed as dividends is closest to:

rationale.A: Correct. The dividend tax applies to after-corporate-tax earnings: 1 − 0.70 × 0.80 = 44.0%.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 50.0% simply adds the two rates, taxing the same unit of earnings twice in full.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 30.0% is the corporate rate only and ignores the shareholder-level dividend tax that double taxation adds.

stem: Last year a firm paid a dividend of USD 0.80 per share. Next year's EPS is expected to be USD 2.50. The firm targets a 45% payout ratio and closes 25% of the gap between its target and its previous dividend each year. The expected dividend next year is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 1.13 is the full target dividend, which assumes immediate (100%) adjustment.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 0.28 = 0.25 × 1.125 applies the adjustment speed to the target and ignores the previous dividend.

stem: A bank's shares trade at USD 18 while its book value per share is USD 24. It repurchases 10% of its shares in the open market using excess cash. The repurchase will most likely cause book value per share to:
explanation: Buying back shares below book value removes less equity per share than each share's book value, so remaining shareholders' BVPS rises.

rationale.A: Incorrect. BVPS falls only when shares are repurchased above book value.
rationale.B: Incorrect. BVPS is unchanged only if the repurchase price equals BVPS.
rationale.C: Correct. Price (18) below BVPS (24) means BVPS increases after the buyback.
